entries.reason: the Tier 2 verdict on Metal/MetalKit: the class and its capture scopes are tooling objects, not GPU work; capturing a trace is what genuinely needs a backend this port does not have
entries.effect: sharedCaptureManager gives a real singleton; newCaptureScopeWithDevice:/newCaptureScopeWithCommandQueue: give a real object conforming to MTLCaptureScope whose beginScope/endScope are no-ops; the deprecated startCaptureWithDevice:/WithCommandQueue:/WithScope: are no-ops and stopCapture is a no-op; isCapturing always answers NO
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the contract

entries.reason: MTLCaptureManager calls it; the protocol status is not pushed onto the class that calls it
entries.effect: the object MTLCaptureManager's -newCaptureScopeWithDevice:/-newCaptureScopeWithCommandQueue: gives conforms to it in full: label, device and commandQueue hold what they were given, beginScope/endScope are no-ops
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the contract
